subject: Hosted billing: monthly cutoff, PO flow, and card failover
messages:
From: Jordan Miller <jordan.miller@acme-corp.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel@redwood.com>
Cc: Finance Ops <finance@acme-corp.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 15:42:00 -0400
Subject: Billing setup questions for Redwood Hosted API

Hi Rachel,

We're getting close to kickoff and my finance team has a few practical questions about how billing will appear and what options we have for initial months:

- Can Redwood consolidate multiple teams under a single monthly invoice or do we need per-project billing?
- What is your invoice cutoff / invoice period? If we go with monthly invoicing, when is the charge captured (day of month or rolling 30d)?
- We prefer to pay by PO/net30. Is that supported for our expected usage band (we're targeting ~$45k/mo in consumption initially)?
- If a card is on file and fails, what's the failover? Will charges be retried or will the invoice be created for manual payment?

I've attached a brief doc with our billing compliance checklist. Happy to hop on a quick call if easier.

Thanks,
Jordan
Jordan Miller
Director, Cloud Product
Acme Corp
[Attachment: acme_billing_requirements.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Rachel Kim <rachel@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Miller <jordan.miller@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 17:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Billing setup questions for Redwood Hosted API

Hi Jordan — thanks for the clear list, this is helpful. Answering inline and including next steps below.

- Consolidation: Yes — we support invoice consolidation across multiple teams under a single billing account. We can map multiple API keys/projects to one invoice ID once the account is provisioned.
- Invoice period & cutoff: Our standard hosted API invoice runs on a calendar-month basis; cutoff is the last UTC day of the month and invoices are issued within the first 3 business days following month-end. We can discuss a custom cutoff if your procurement needs differ.
- PO / net terms: For customer commitments at your scale we can enable net30 on a monthly invoicing cadence; that requires a quick underwriting step and an executed MSA/Order Form. Net terms are tied to the billing account and will apply to consolidated invoices.
- Card failover: If a card is on file and a charge fails, our Collections policy will automatically create an invoice and notify billing contacts; we run 3 retries over a 7-day window before opening a collections case. For customers on net terms, we typically do a PO-first model (no auto-charge) unless you ask us to keep a backup card on file.

Next steps I propose:
1) I'll send a one-page billing checklist and the hosted ratecard (attached).
2) Ben from GTM will confirm the underwriting steps and lead the PO setup.
3) If you want net30, please have your procurement sign the attached order form and return to finance@redwood.com.

Would you be open to a 20-minute call tomorrow to finalize the flow?

Best,
Rachel
Rachel Kim
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Redwood_ratecard_v1.xlsx]

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Billing setup questions for Redwood Hosted API

Rachel / Karthik — looping in Finance to confirm the underwriting checklist and expected timeline for net30 enablement for ACME. Quick notes:

- Underwriting pieces we need from Acme: signed Order Form, PO number, and a W-9 (US). For larger accounts we also ask for three months of bank references if requested by finance.
- Typical lead time: 5-7 business days from receipt of completed forms and PO.
- If Acme wants card fallback, we need explicit approval in the order form and a signed PCI attestation for card storage.

Karthik, can you confirm whether we need to open a payment terms exception for the 30d net and what thresholds trigger a contract review?

Thanks — Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Sales Ops, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel@redwood.com>, Jordan Miller <jordan.miller@acme-corp.com>
Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Billing setup questions for Redwood Hosted API

Jordan — thanks for the questions and for the checklist. We can do net30 on a consolidated monthly invoice for the $45k/mo band. A few administrative points:

- Please return the signed order form with PO number to finance@redwood.com.
- Once received, Finance will issue the first consolidated invoice for the current month on the 3rd business day after month-end; payment will be due net30 from the invoice date.
- If you want the backup card route, include the checkbox on the order form; otherwise we will treat invoices as manual pay with collections retry behavior as Rachel described.

I'm available Mon/Tue afternoon if you want to confirm details on a call.

Best regards,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
